project_name: Add Distributed Support - MirDB Raft Consensus

scenarios.name: Cluster Formation and Leader Election
scenarios.description: Validate that multiple nodes can form a cluster and elect a leader automatically

steps.action: Start multiple nodes with valid cluster configuration
steps.description: Start 3 instances of MirDB nodes with cluster configuration pointing to the same cluster
steps.context: Using TOML config files with node IDs, peers list, and Raft parameters

steps.action: Wait for cluster formation and leader election
steps.description: Wait up to 5 seconds for nodes to discover each other and elect a leader
steps.context: Uses Raft election timeout and voting mechanism

steps.description: Query each node's health endpoint to confirm exactly one leader and followers
steps.context: Leader should respond with leader status, followers with follower status

test_cases.input: GET /status on all 3 nodes after startup
test_cases.expected: Exactly 1 node returns 'leader' state and 2 nodes return 'follower' state within 5 seconds
All nodes report consistent cluster membership list with 3 nodes
Elects leader successfully and forms consensus group

scenarios.name: Automatic Leader Failover
scenarios.description: Verify cluster automatically detects leader failure and elects new leader

steps.description: Create a 3-node cluster with elected leader and active replication
steps.context: Cluster should be in steady state with healthy follower replication

steps.description: Kill or disconnect the leader node from the cluster
steps.context: Simulates network partition or node crash

steps.description: Monitor remaining nodes for new leader election
steps.context: Election timeout triggers on followers, new leader should be elected

steps.description: Confirm writes succeed on new leader and cluster remains available
steps.context: New leader should handle writes and replicate to remaining follower

test_cases.expected: New leader elected within 500ms of failure detection

test_cases.input: Send SET command to cluster during failover
test_cases.expected: Before failover: success; During election: may timeout; After election: success to new leader
All previously committed writes are preserved and available on new leader

scenarios.name: Write Operation with Quorum Consensus
scenarios.description: Validate that write operations are replicated to majority before acknowledgment

steps.description: Create stable cluster with elected leader
steps.context: Leader has 2 followers replicating data

steps.description: Send SET command with key-value pair via memcached protocol
steps.context: Client connects to leader node or gets redirected

steps.description: Leader replicates to followers and waits for majority acknowledgment
steps.context: Majority = 2 of 3 nodes including leader

steps.description: Confirm write is persisted on multiple nodes
steps.context: Query data from followers to verify replication

test_cases.expected: Returns STORED after quorum (2/3 nodes) acknowledgment within 10ms

test_cases.input: GET key from all 3 nodes (including followers)
test_cases.expected: All nodes return the same value (eventual consistency within 100ms)

test_cases.input: Kill leader immediately after SET acknowledgment
test_cases.expected: Write is preserved and available on new leader (2 of 3 nodes had the data)
Writes require acknowledgment from 3/5 nodes (majority)

scenarios.name: Log Replication Consistency
scenarios.description: Verify Raft log replication maintains consistency across nodes

steps.description: Send sequence of SET commands (10-20 operations) to create log entries
steps.context: Each write creates a log entry with monotonically increasing index

steps.description: Check that follower logs match leader log order and content
steps.context: Use status endpoints to query log index positions

steps.description: Ensure committed entries (majority acknowledged) are not lost
steps.context: Committed entries must be durable and replicated

steps.description: Temporarily slow network to one follower, then restore
steps.context: Follower should catch up without skipping or duplicating entries

test_cases.expected: All followers receive log entries in same order with matching term/index
Committed log entries are identical across all nodes

test_cases.input: Block network to follower, send 10 writes, restore network
test_cases.expected: Follower catches up without data loss, maintains log consistency

scenarios.name: Cluster Health Monitoring Endpoints
scenarios.description: Test cluster status and health monitoring capabilities

steps.action: Start cluster and wait for stability
steps.description: Create 3-node cluster with elected leader
steps.context: Cluster should be operational and replicating data

steps.description: Send GET request to /status or /info endpoint
steps.context: Endpoint should return cluster health information

steps.description: Check that response includes leader info, followers, and replication status
steps.context: Information should be accurate and complete

steps.description: Check status endpoint during leader failure and election
steps.context: Status should reflect changing cluster state accurately

test_cases.expected: Returns JSON with: node_id, role (leader/follower), leader_id, peers list, term, log index
Returns health status: 'healthy' if leader elected and followers replicating, 'degraded' if missing nodes
Returns replication lag in ms and lag in log entries (last_applied - last_sent)

scenarios.name: Follower Reads for Read Scaling
scenarios.description: Test eventually-consistent read operations from follower nodes

steps.description: Create 3-node cluster and write test data via leader
steps.context: Ensure data is replicated to followers

steps.description: Send GET command with eventual_consistency parameter
steps.context: Client should be able to specify consistency level

steps.description: Check that followers respond to read requests
steps.context: Follower should check its local state machine (DataManager)

steps.description: Ensure read reflects data within acceptable lag threshold
steps.context: Should not return stale data beyond NFR-4 threshold (100ms)

test_cases.input: GET key with eventual_consistency=true from follower
test_cases.expected: Returns data with replication lag < 100ms

test_cases.input: Send read to all followers simultaneously
test_cases.expected: All followers return consistent results within allowed lag window

test_cases.input: Write data, immediately read from follower with forced_lag_check
test_cases.expected: Follower either returns value or indicates 'not yet committed' with appropriate status

scenarios.name: Snapshot-Based State Transfer
scenarios.description: Test efficient state transfer using snapshots for lagging followers

steps.description: Start cluster, write significant data (10MB+), then start new follower
steps.context: New follower is significantly behind leader's log position

steps.description: Leader detects follower lag and sends snapshot instead of log replay
steps.context: Snapshot should include LSM tree state (memtable + SSTables)

steps.description: Track snapshot creation, transfer, and application on follower
steps.context: Should include metadata about SSTables and their levels

steps.description: After snapshot, follower should continue with incremental log entries
steps.context: Follower should reach caught-up state and maintain consistency

test_cases.input: Start new follower on cluster with 50MB+ of data
test_cases.expected: Leader sends snapshot, follower applies it within reasonable time
Snapshot includes all memtable data and SSTable manifests for full recovery
Data checksums match, follower state matches leader state after application

scenarios.name: Memcached Protocol Compatibility
scenarios.description: Ensure existing memcached clients work unchanged with distributed MirDB

steps.description: Deploy 3-node cluster with leader election
steps.context: Cluster should be ready to accept memcached connections

steps.description: Use existing memcached client library (Python, Java, etc.)
steps.context: No special configuration or code changes needed

steps.description: Run SET, GET, DELETE, ADD, REPLACE, APPEND, PREPEND commands
steps.context: Commands should follow standard memcached protocol

steps.description: Test that clients are redirected to leader when connecting to follower
steps.context: Redirect should be transparent to client (if supported) or require client retry

test_cases.input: SET key=value using standard memcached client
test_cases.expected: Returns 'STORED' response, same as single-node MirDB

test_cases.input: GET key from same or different client connection
test_cases.expected: Returns stored value with standard memcached response format

test_cases.input: Connect to follower, send SET command
test_cases.expected: Returns 'LEADER_REDIRECT <leader_host:port>' or transparently forwards (based on implementation)

test_cases.input: Run concurrent SET operations from multiple clients
test_cases.expected: All commands succeed and data is consistent across cluster

scenarios.name: Network Partition Recovery
scenarios.description: Verify system survives and recovers from network partitions without data loss

steps.description: Start 5 nodes and ensure they're stable with replicated data
steps.context: Larger cluster allows testing split scenarios

steps.description: Separate cluster into two groups (3 nodes and 2 nodes)
steps.context: Group with majority (3 nodes) should continue; minority should stop accepting writes

steps.description: Confirm minority group stops processing writes
steps.context: Raft requires majority for leader election and log commitment

steps.description: Reconnect partitioned groups and allow re-convergence
steps.context: Raft should handle reconciliation without data loss

test_cases.expected: Group with 3 nodes maintains leader and continues operations; group with 2 nodes stops accepting writes

test_cases.input: Send writes to both partition groups
test_cases.expected: Only majority group accepts and commits writes; minority group rejects with appropriate error
Minority group converges to majority state, updating with committed entries; no committed data lost

scenarios.name: Raft Log Persistence and Recovery
scenarios.description: Verify Raft log survives node restarts and maintains durability

steps.action: Create cluster and generate log entries
steps.description: Start 3-node cluster and perform multiple write operations to create raft log entries
steps.context: Log entries represent committed writes that must persist

steps.description: Shutdown leader to simulate planned maintenance
steps.context: Graceful shutdown should flush and persist logs

steps.description: Bring the node back online with persisted log data
steps.context: Node should recover and rejoin as follower with preserved log state

steps.description: Confirm node recovered with all committed log entries intact
steps.context: Rejoined node should have consistent log with other members

test_cases.input: Write 50 key-value pairs, stop leader, restart
test_cases.expected: After restart, node rejoins cluster and all 50 writes are still present and accessible
Node recovers without corruption, continues replication from last committed index
After power restore and restart, node recovers with raft log persisted on disk, no data loss

scenarios.name: Performance - Write Latency with Consensus
scenarios.description: Measure write latency impact from Raft consensus compared to single-node operation

steps.description: Measure baseline SET command latency on single MirDB instance
steps.context: Single-node provides baseline without consensus overhead

steps.description: Measure SET command latency on distributed cluster with same workload
steps.context: Consensus adds network RTT for majority acknowledgment

steps.description: Calculate latency increase and throughput impact
steps.context: Performance should meet success metrics (< 2x latency increase)

steps.description: Run sustained write workload (1000+ operations) to measure consistent performance
steps.context: Ensure performance doesn't degrade over time

test_cases.input: Measure latency for 1000 SET operations on single node
test_cases.expected: Baseline p50 < 1ms, p99 < 5ms on local SSD

test_cases.input: Measure latency for 1000 SET operations on 3-node cluster
test_cases.expected: p50 < 2ms (within 2x), p99 < 10ms, achieves consensus for writes within 10ms
System maintains 10,000 ops/sec throughput (10k QPS target)

scenarios.description: Validate cluster configuration and deployment scenarios

steps.description: Parse cluster configuration from TOML file
steps.context: Configuration should include node_id, peers, raft parameters

steps.description: Ensure configuration has valid format, node IDs, and peer lists
steps.context: Invalid config should prevent startup with clear error

steps.description: Test support for different cluster sizes (3, 5, 7 nodes)
steps.context: All sizes should form valid clusters

test_cases.input: Start node with valid TOML config containing 3 peers
test_cases.expected: Node starts successfully and begins discovery process

test_cases.input: Start node with invalid config (duplicate node IDs)
test_cases.expected: Node fails to start with clear error message indicating invalid configuration
Forms consensus group and can survive up to 3 node failures

scenarios.name: Error Handling and Edge Cases
scenarios.description: Test error conditions and edge cases in distributed operations

steps.description: Send write requests to cluster during ongoing leader election
steps.context: System should handle gracefully with appropriate error responses

steps.action: Test cluster with single node failure
steps.description: Kill one node in 3-node cluster, verify continued operation with quorum
steps.context: 3-node cluster can survive 1 failure (N/2 rounded down)

steps.description: Kill 2 nodes in 3-node cluster, preventing majority
steps.context: Should reject writes with appropriate error, maintain safety

steps.description: Send same write operation twice due to client retry
steps.context: Raft should handle idempotently and not create duplicates

test_cases.expected: Returns SERVER_ERROR with 'no leader elected' or equivalent
Cluster continues to accept writes with 2-node majority
Remaining node rejects writes with 'insufficient quorum' error

test_cases.input: Retry SET command 3 times with same key-value
test_cases.expected: Only one entry in log, no duplicate keys with different values
